accuracy.evidence: Checked against the PSHE Association KS3 Programme of Study (2020) Health and Wellbeing strand on identity, self-concept, self-esteem and how social media affects self-image, and the DfE (2019) RSE and Health Education guidance on friendships and online life. Social identity theory is credited to Tajfel and Turner (1979) and the identity versus role confusion stage to Erikson (1968). The personal vs social identity split matches those sources, and no claim goes past them.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets four slips named in the adult text and tested in the lab: identity as one fixed label (web predict 'One main thing', timeline 'She was fake at 8'), fitting in treated as belonging (Kai predict, Leah challenge item, m6), upward social comparison with curated feeds (post-flip step, Ravi item), and assuming influences are only personal choice (the roots step traces family, peer and media influences).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagbelong uses mechanics no other lab shares: a two-ring identity web you drop parts onto (inner personal, outer groups), a source-tracing grid, a draggable dot on a fitting-in/belonging track, post cards that flip to show what's behind them while a mood meter rises, and a scrubbable age 8/12/16 timeline that redraws Jo's interests, groups and values. The 30% shingle gate passed against all labs, including the P&S labs for friendship and self-reflection.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each step builds one idea used in the next: identity has personal and social parts (web), those parts have influences (roots), groups can demand fitting in or offer belonging (track), media comparison skews self-image (posts), and identity develops over time (timeline). The values row stays the same across ages while interests and groups change, so the learner sees the point before the text states it.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with plausible wrong answers: 'one thing or many?' (One main thing), 'Kai changes how he acts... is that belonging?' (Yes, he is in the group), 'why might Jo feel worse after scrolling?' (Her life really is worse) and 'interests at 16 differ from 8' (She was fake at 8). Each is tested straight away by its step, and the kit's reveal confirms or corrects the choice.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions (orchestra vs traits, Leah's headscarf, media advert vs grandad's cooking, Ravi's holiday photos, Mo switching to coding club, where you truly belong). Each has shuffled buttons and nine m= messages tied to the wrong choice, e.g. 'Sharing a band with friends is a friends (peer) influence' and 'Trying to beat their post keeps the comparison going'.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores FK grade 4.4 (learner limit 6.5) with concrete examples such as laughing at cruel jokes and a choir that welcomes quiet and silly days. Adult text scores 8.0 (limit 9.5) after splitting long sentences. It names the KS3 terms self-concept, self-esteem, social identity, influences and social comparison, and the canvas text is 12 to 15 px on phones.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph does one job: define personal and social identity, list the four influences with examples, separate fitting in from belonging, and explain feeds and changing interests. The family tip is a concrete two-ring drawing activity with two talk prompts, and the filler-phrase gate passed.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark after Show me on every step: the first pass had personal tags overlapping the centre label, so the inner tags were restacked vertically under 'Personal'. Group tags sit on the middle of the outer ring, the track lists Kai/Priya/Sam/Ellie under each side, and the timeline dots are 9 to 14 px with 40 px vertical hit bands. All canvas actions also have buttons (Inner ring, Outer ring, the four influences, Fitting in or Belonging, Look behind, and an age button for each age).

accessibility.evidence: The pipeline browser walk ran axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors. The canvas aria-label repeats the live prompt or feedback (e.g. 'Moment 1: Kai laughs at jokes he finds mean... Drag the dot left for fitting in or right for belonging.'), and every drag or tap has a labelled button, including 'Personal identity: <part>' labels.

sources: PSHE Association (2020) Programme of Study for PSHE Education, Key Stages 1-5: KS3 Health and Wellbeing (self-concept, identity, social media)
DfE (2019) Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education and Health Education statutory guidance
Tajfel, H. & Turner, J. C. (1979) An integrative theory of intergroup conflict (social identity theory)
Erikson, E. H. (1968) Identity: Youth and Crisis, Norton
Festinger, L. (1954) A theory of social comparison processes, Human Relations 7(2)
